description: Three-panel composite of mechanical-property curves for a low-carbon low-density cryogenic steel tested at RT and LNT; in every panel the black curve is labelled RT and the red curve LNT. (a) Tensile engineering stress-strain curves, x = Engineering strain 0.0-0.8, y = Engineering stress (MPa) 0-1000: the RT curve yields near 250 MPa and peaks just under the 600 MPa gridline before failing near strain 0.52, while the LNT curve reaches just below 950 MPa and fails near strain 0.75. (b) Twin-axis plot, x = True strain 0.0-0.6, y = "True stress/strain hardening rate (MPa)" 0-4000, showing true stress-strain curves (lower pair) plus strain hardening rate curves (upper pair); the RT hardening rate descends from about 2500 MPa with markers A and A', whereas the LNT rate starts near 4000 MPa and falls step-wise through markers B, C0, C1, C, C2 and D to about 1500 MPa, with arrows and dashed vertical guides. (c) Instrumented Charpy impact: force-displacement (left axis Force/kN, 0-20) and energy-displacement (right axis "KV2/J", 0-350) versus Displacement/mm 0-30, a vertical line marking Fm; printed annotations give Wm = 79.28 J and Wp = 251.33 J (black, RT) and Wm = 99.19 J, Wp = 156.71 J (red, LNT). Together the panels argue that cryogenic deformation raises both strength and ductility while impact energy transfers from crack propagation to crack initiation.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots two engineering stress-strain curves, black labelled RT and red labelled LNT, over engineering strain 0.0-0.8 and engineering stress 0-1000 MPa; the LNT curve lies above the RT curve over the whole strain range.

In (a) the RT curve peaks between the 400 and 600 MPa gridlines (closer to 600) and terminates near engineering strain 0.52, while the LNT curve peaks just below the 1000 MPa gridline and terminates near strain 0.75.

Panel (b) uses a single ordinate labelled 'True stress/strain hardening rate (MPa)' spanning 0-4000, containing both the true stress-strain curves (lower pair) and the strain hardening rate curves (upper pair) against true strain 0.0-0.6.

In (b) the LNT strain hardening rate curve starts near the top of the 4000 MPa axis and descends through labelled markers B, C0, C1, C, C2 and D, ending near 1500 MPa, staying above the RT hardening rate curve throughout.
In (b) the RT curve is annotated with markers A and A' and the LNT curve with B, C0, C1, C, C2 and D, each accompanied by an arrow and a dashed vertical guide line.
In (c) the RT force-displacement curve peaks near 14 kN whereas the LNT force-displacement curve peaks near 19-20 kN, and Fm is marked by a dashed vertical line near 5-7 mm displacement.
In (c) the RT energy curve (black) rises steadily to roughly 250 J on the right-hand KV2/J axis at large displacement, while the LNT energy curve (red) saturates at a lower value near 160 J.
Panel (c) prints Wm = 79.28 J and Wp = 251.33 J in black (RT) and Wm = 99.19 J and Wp = 156.71 J in red (LNT).

The caption states (b) presents true stress-strain curves and corresponding strain hardening rate curves, and that the strain hardening behaviour is split into two stages at RT and four stages at LNT.

The citing text states the 0.2 % offset yield strength rises from 251 to 497 MPa and the ultimate tensile strength from 580 to 945 MPa as temperature decreases from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperature.
The citing text states the uniform elongation increases from 38.5 % to 56.0 % and the total elongation from 52.0 % to 75.5 % between RT and LNT.
The citing text states the Charpy V-notch impact energy is 331 ± 4 J at room temperature and 254 ± 6 J at cryogenic temperature.

The citing text states crack initiation energy is nearly the same (~80-100 J) at both temperatures, while crack propagation energy drops from 251 J at RT to 156 J at LNT, so impact behaviour is governed by crack propagation.
The citing text states the work hardening rate at LNT is much higher than at RT, attributed to increased lattice friction stress (143 MPa at RT versus 389 MPa at LNT).

subfigures.description: Tensile engineering stress-strain curves, black RT and red LNT, over engineering strain 0.0-0.8 and engineering stress 0-1000 MPa. RT yields near 250 MPa and peaks just below 600 MPa with failure around strain 0.52; LNT peaks just below 950 MPa and fails near strain 0.75.

Twin-axis plot of true stress-strain curves (lower pair) and corresponding strain hardening rate curves (upper pair) versus true strain 0.0-0.6, y-label 'True stress/strain hardening rate (MPa)' 0-4000. Stage markers A, A' on the RT curves and B, C0, C1, C, C2, D on the LNT curves, marked with arrows and dashed vertical lines; LNT hardening rate stays well above the RT one.

Instrumented Charpy impact curves: force-displacement (left axis Force/kN 0-20) and energy-displacement (right axis KV2/J 0-350) versus displacement 0-30 mm, black RT and red LNT. A dashed vertical line marks Fm; annotations read Wm=79.28J, Wp=251.33J (RT) and Wm=99.19J, Wp=156.71J (LNT).
